name: 1637 Prairie Avenue — Jesse Spalding's remodel of the Grosvenor house, K01 frontage assembly

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the K01 main body at its north (low-v) side: the draft's origin moved 1.04 m north along its own frame, onto the north wall of the 1911 sheet's traced main part (s20fp-1637-b1), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check, so its own fit residual, 2.46 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation 179.603 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line, so v runs south.
placement.symbolic_location: 1637 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1637 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).

footprint.note: The main body read off the 1911 sheet's trace (s20fp-1637-b1) in the lot frame: the north part's brick front at 11.0 m from its rear wall, the north wall at v 0 and the south wall at 13.1, so 11.0 m deep and 13.1 m along the front, the trace's own width where the draft's 0.25 m cell fit stopped at 11.5 m. The sheet's south 4.8 m stands 1.0 m forward of the north part: the engraving's wing, built on it as a K08 projection (form.bays). The range behind the south part is a rear wing (form.rear_wings); the sheet's frame porch across the north part and its small canted bay on the wing are the 1911 state's and are not built (T-2442 weighs them).

stories.note: Two full storeys over a raised basement, with the roof storey lit by its dormers: the engraving's own count (the basement's lights at the walk, the principal storey's tall windows and the wing's French window, the second storey under the cornice). The 1911 sheet prints '2½B', the same count with the half storey in the roof.

construction.note: The 1911 sheet colours the house brick; the engraving draws every face it shows in coursed brick, the bay and the wing included.

principal_floor_m.note: 2.3 m over grade, read through the engraving's camera (data/reference_views/spalding_house_1637_prairie/spalding_remodel_engraving.json) off the wing's balcony floor and the stoop's head (y 668 px): a raised basement whose lights stand a full storey at the walk. Above the K01 contract's 0.8-1.8 m starting range, so it stands on the engraving.

storey_heights_m.note: Floor to floor, principal storey first: 4.3 m and 4.9 m. Through the engraving's camera the second floor falls at about 6.6 m (between the principal windows' heads at 5.7-6.0 m and the second storey's sills at 7.2-7.4 m) and the cornice's soffit at about 11.5 m. No dimension is printed on the engraving.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A brick-and-a-half wall, as every K01 brick house's.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: A brick-and-a-half wall, as every K01 brick house's.

service_wall_brick.note: The one K03 panel k03_brick lays; the engraving's brick is monochrome.

street_front_trim.note: Plain flat stone lintels on both storeys: the engraving draws the windows as plain square-headed holes in the brick with no hoods. The heavy surrounds and sills it hatches are listed open.

wall_head.note: A heavy cornice over a plain frieze runs round the front, the bay and the wing at one height in the engraving; drawn as K10's bracketed timber cornice, the kit's one heavy eave. The wing carries the same cornice (T-2467): the engraving draws its cornice as a band as deep as the main one's (y 232-262 px) with a block in it over the window, where T-2465's crown carried K05's 0.2 m fascia alone. The wing's walls rise into the crown's soffit, so K10's brackets and bed moulding run round its three faces on the main wall head's line (`crown`): two on its cheek off the front, clear of the front's own, eight on its face and two on its far cheek, which runs on into the side wall's. Through the camera the wing's band now spans y 258-265 px at the fascia's top to 293-299 at the brackets' feet, 35 px, as the main cornice's does (258-293), where the fascia alone was 9 px. The block (`crown.block`) stands on the window's centre, 0.75 m wide, from the brackets' feet through the fascia to 0.15 m over its top and 0.05 m past its face: through the camera at x 709-738 px against the engraving's about 700-730, rising about 6 px over the band as the engraving's does about 5-7. Its width, rise and projection are read off the plate at the wing's scale (about 0.023 m/px), not measured; the whole band stands about 30 px under the engraving's, which is the house's eave height (the match record's open item), not the wing's.

roof_form.note: The engraving's main roof is steep and slated, with gabled dormers in its street and north faces and a level top line: a mansard's steep lower faces under a low upper hip. K01's hip runs its ridge from the front to the rear and needs side walls longer than the front, which this 13.1 m front on an 11.0 m depth does not have.

roof_pitch_deg.note: The upper hip over the curb, which no picture shows: the engraving draws a level top line with nothing over it, so the hip is laid at 10 degrees, the foot of K05's mansard_upper starting range, which from the camera's eye rises about as steeply as the sightline to the curb and so stays behind it (T-2452; it was 18 degrees).

eave_overhang_m.note: The cornice's projection, inside the draft rules' range; the engraving's cornice stands about half a metre proud.

stair_tread_m.note: The floor of the K01 contract's tread range, a steep stoop (T-2535; RECONSTRUCTED, bounded by the drawn foot): the engraving draws the flight's foot at the fence's first post (x 557 px), and through its camera that column at the stoop's north cheek (s 5.05) stands at u 15.35, 4.35 m before the main front. Fourteen risers of 0.164 m (K07's whole-riser solve of the 2.3 m principal floor) on thirteen 0.25 m goings and a 1.1 m landing reach exactly that far; at 0.3 m the foot stood at 5.1 m (x 586 px). The going itself is not drawn: it is the shortest the contract allows, chosen because the engraving's foot asks for it.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: A landing at the door, 1.1 m deep (T-2535, RECONSTRUCTED and bounded by the drawn foot; 1.2 m, as 1620's, until then): with the 0.25 m going it puts the flight's foot 4.35 m before the front, under the engraving's first fence post (x 557 px) on the stoop's north cheek. The engraving draws the landing's rail but not its depth.

stoop_width_m.note: The engraving's stoop between its rails, about the door's width and a jamb each side.

entrance_bay.note: The door stands between the swell bay and the wing, under one window of the second storey and a dormer, as the engraving draws it; the bay and the wing stand over the front's two outer bays.

front_bays.note: Bay centres along the street front, north to south: the swell bay's centre (2.72 m), the door's (6.25 m, read through the engraving's camera at x 515 px), and the wing's (10.7 m, the middle of the sheet's 4.8 m step). The windows K01 would cut in the outer two bays stand behind the bay and the wing, which carry their own.

side_bays.note: Window centres along the north flank, rear to front: the two the engraving shows over the garden wall at about u 0.6-1.8 and 6.3-6.7 m, the rear one moved in to 1.6 m so its lintel clears the rear corner.

north_bays.note: The south wall, which no picture shows, stands near the lot line with 1639: left blind.

rear_bays.note: Two windows a storey on the rear wall beside the rear range, which no picture shows.

sash_by_storey.note: The engraving's windows read about 1 m wide; the principal storey's about 2.9 m tall over a 0.7 m sill, held to the K01 contract's 2.4 m clear height (listed open), the second storey's 2.3 m over a 0.6 m sill.

basement_lights.note: The basement's lights stand nearly a storey at the walk in the engraving (about 0.5-1.9 m over grade under the bay). The front's own two outer bays stand behind the swell bay and the wing, so K01 cuts none of these: the bay and the wing carry the engraving's basement lights themselves (T-2535, form.bays).

roof_covering.note: The engraving's lower faces are laid in slate; the upper hip, which it does not show, is painted tin, as 1620's mansard.

mansard.note: Steep straight lower faces 2.6 m tall from the cornice to the curb (the engraving's level top line at about 14.1 m over grade): K05's convex variant laid with no bulge (T-2452), since the engraving draws each face as one plane from the cornice to the top line, hipped at the corners, at 65 degrees, the floor of K05's mansard starting range (the engraving's hip ends lean back further, by its draughtsman's perspective an amount not read). Three dormers where the engraving draws them: two on the street face, over the swell bay (2.8 m) and over the door (6.25 m), and one on the north face 6.3 m from the rear. Each is the engraving's gabled dormer (T-2452): a square-headed two-over-two sash 0.9 by 1.2 m in a stone face 1.6 m wide (the street ones about 70 px across at the front's 0.023 m/px), its face standing nearly on the fascia so its sill is about the cornice's height (11.7 m against the engraving's about 11.5 m), and a 40 degree pediment to an apex at about 13.9 m (the engraving's about 13.5 m, just under the top line), its cheeks and slopes slated as the lower faces are. The sash, the surround and the pitch are read off the plate at its scale, not measured. The record's 'south' face is the K01 frame's v-0 side, which on this side of the avenue is the north wall. The wing's own roof (T-2465) is the crown: K01's mansard crown (T-2404's) built as a hip over the south wing, its plan the wing's 4.8 m front and junctions run 5.5 m back into the main roof, its cornice 0.55 m past the wing's face and its fascia's top on the main eave. The engraving draws the wing hipped to a ridge running back into the main roof, its apex at about 14.4 m through the camera (y 142 px), a little over the main roof's level top line; the sides and back at 45.5 degrees put the ridge at 14.5 m (y 137 px), and the street end at 60 degrees keeps that end in front of the main lower faces up to the curb, as the engraving draws it whole. The pitches are chosen to those two readings and to K04's rule that a face over 45 degrees is slated, not measured; the depth is unseen.

chimneys.note: Three stacks where the engraving draws them, each at the top it reads through the camera: two on the north wall's cornice, near its front (u 9.2 m, top 16.4 m over grade) and near its rear (3.2 m, 15.5 m), and one over the wing. T-2465 stood the wing's stack beside its hipped roof's ridge, where the engraving draws it just south of the apex: its shaft at x 662-715 px through the camera against the drawn 663-717 (u 10.2, v 11.2, 0.5 m south of the ridge line) and its top at 15.11 m (y 112 px against the drawn 113), the least that clears the crown's 14.5 m ridge by 0.6 m. T-2471 dresses the three from the K15 chimney kit (chimneys.k15), as the engraving draws them panelled and capped: each takes the kit's carved form (k15.stack.sherman) less the stone bands and corbel blocks the engraving does not draw, so three corbelled brick courses under a 0.14 m stone cap projecting 0.15 m, the stack turned so its panelled faces face the street and the rear. The two tall stacks on the north wall carry a sunk panel 0.45 m wide on those faces, run from 0.5 m over the highest roof under the stack to 0.3 m under its head (1.87 m on the front one, 0.97 m on the rear one), where the engraving draws the tall front stack's lit face as a long light field in a dark border; the wing's stack stands too little over its crown's covering for one and is left plain (panelled: false). Two flues each, the kit's 0.21 m liner. The kit's flashing is not laid: it reads one slope, and these stand on the cornice and on the crown's steep side, so each joins its roof as the plain stack did. The courses, cap, panel sizes and flues are the kit's or read off the plate at its scale, not measured. Each top was read at the drawn top, which is a dark hooded crown over the cap (a pot or a cowl, about 0.4-0.5 m), not built.

rainwater.note: No picture shows a pipe, and the engraving's street front has none between its bay and wing: two down the north flank, at its rear and front ends, and one at the rear wall's north corner.

window_kit.note: Two-over-two sashes, the kit's sash for a brick front of the 1880s; the engraving's glazing bars are not legible.

entrance_kit.note: A panelled door up a stoop between rails, as the engraving draws it between the bay and the wing; the yard runs 10.2 m to the street line (the draft's street_u). T-2447: the landing and the flight are railed with a turned balustrade on each cheek, 1.0 m over the landing, as the engraving draws the landing's rail (y 623-675 px over the stoop's head at 668 px); its balusters' profile is the K07 kit's and RECONSTRUCTED.

windows.why_not_ordinary: the basement light under the bow, read off the engraving: about 1.3 m tall over a 0.5 m sill, barred, under a flat head, under the middle window (T-2535)

the wing's two round-headed basement lights, read off the engraving: each about 0.9 m wide and 1.4 m to its crown over a 0.3 m sill, 0.7 m apart, under the French window; each drawn with an upright bar and a cross bar, so a two-light sash under a fanlight, K06's round-headed parlour window at a basement light's size (T-2535)

bays.note: The engraving's two outer bays, on the 1911 sheet's plan. North: a swell bay from grade nearly to the cornice, 4.8 m on its chord from 0.3 m inside the north corner to the door's jamb, about 1.3 m out, three windows a storey (read at about -31, 20 and 48 degrees round it through the camera, set at -36, 2 and 40 so the outer two keep their recesses clear of the front wall where the bow runs back into it). South: the wing, on the sheet's 4.8 m by 1.0 m step flush with the south corner, one window a storey on its centre, the principal storey's a French window over a balcony in the engraving (a sash here; the balcony is T-2442's). The bay rises from grade to the cornice itself, as the engraving carries it (T-2472): its upper storey 4.64 m, so its wall top stands at 11.24 m, the foot of K10's bed moulding (T-2528: 4.552 m and 11.152 m until the soffit was read off the mansard's wall head), and its eaves ARE the cornice, carried round the bow (`eaves.cornice`): the bed moulding swept round its plan under the house's soffit (11.3 m) and fascia (to 11.5 m), 0.5 m out from the bow's face as the main eave stands from the wall, in the same painted timber; the wall's bed moulding stops at the bow's junctions and its brackets stand clear of them. The bow carries no brackets of its own: the engraving draws its top as one plain band, and its brackets would be K10's, not the engraving's. Through the camera that band lands at y 245-267 px on the bow's crown, the engraving's at about 255-270; until T-2472 the bay stopped at 10.7 m under a plain K08 eave (y 270-287 px). The wing is carried up to the cornice (T-2465): its upper storey 4.75 m, so its walls stand to 11.35 m, 0.05 m into the soffit of the hipped crown that is its own roof (mansard.crown), where the engraving draws the wing's cornice level with the main one's; its K08 deck and eaves stand inside that crown, and K10's bed moulding runs into its cheeks. Under each, the engraving's basement lights (T-2535), each bay's basement a storey of its own up to the principal floor (2.3 m), as 1621's bow's is, over a 0.1 m plinth (the kit's 0.6 m plinth would stand over the lights' sills; reconstructed), read through its camera on the bay's and the wing's faces: under the bow one barred, flat-headed light at x 388-439 px, y 696-757 px, which reads s 2.57-3.78 and 0.52-1.82 m over grade, so 1.0 m wide and 1.3 m tall over a 0.5 m sill, set under the middle window at the same 2 degrees (the engraving's column, x 413 px, is the middle window's own, x 412); under the wing two round-headed lights at x 675-710 and 736-771 px, y 692-757 px, each about 0.9 m wide on the wing's face with a 0.7 m pier between, 1.4 m to the crown over a 0.3 m sill. The pair's centre reads about 0.35 m south of the wing's (x 723 px against the window's 708), the draughtsman's perspective converging faster than the camera's (the solve's own note), so the pair is centred under the window above, 0.8 m either side. Their glazing bars and the bow light's iron are K06's and K08's, RECONSTRUCTED (L-k01-1637-basement-lights-2535).

rear_wings.note: The 1911 sheet's range behind the south part of the main body (s20fp-1637-b1, from 5.2 m to the south wall and 5.7 m back), two storeys under a flat tin deck; no picture shows it, so its storeys and windows are reconstructed.

boundary.note: T-2447: the engraving's front garden. It draws a tall brick garden wall before the north flank, ending in a square pier before the swell bay (x 357 px), and an iron spear fence from the stoop's foot (a tall post at x 557 px) south before the wing to x 847 px; between them the stoop's own flight comes down to the walk. Both stand close before the house, not on the street line: their feet read on the camera's ground plane at u 13.8-15.6 (y 777-787 px), while the engraving's walk edge reads at u 19-23 (y 800-810 px), where the 1911 sheet puts the street line (u 21.2). So they are built on one line 3.5 m before the main front (u 14.5), on which the wall's end pier projects to x 357 px, exactly the drawn one. The wall is the K11 kit's brick wall with piers, 2.0 m high with piers 2.25 m, its pier at s 0.87 and its north end on the lot line (s -3.138, the 1911 parcel prairie_1637 in this frame): the drawn wall's top (y 680-685 px) reads 2.2 m over grade at the pier. The engraving draws the wall running on north past the frame, which this camera puts about 3.5 m beyond the lot line, onto the unbuilt strip prairie_1625_1637_c; T-2443 rules on that ground, so the wall stops at the lot line here. The fence is the kit's spear fence on its curb, from the stoop's south cheek (s 7.55) to the lot line (s 14.1), its top rail raised to 1.65 m over the curb, 1.9 m over grade, as drawn (y 690 px). Its pickets are the kit's 0.125 m pitch where the engraving draws one about every 0.22 m, an engraver's economy, not a measurement. Iron, brick, coping, curb, pier caps and the wall's end on the lot line are the kit's and RECONSTRUCTED (L-k01-1637-spalding-garden-2447).

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '2½B brick dwelling (D) with a frame (yellow) bay and porches on the Prairie face'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

citations.citation: [The Grosvenor house, 1637 S. Prairie Avenue, as remodeled by Jesse Spalding.] Line engraving of the house from the north-west across Prairie Avenue; unknown illustrator, source publication not named, undated (after the Spalding remodelling, probably 1880s-1890s). Reproduced by the Glessner House Museum, 'The Early History of Prairie Avenue - Part IV', The Story of a House (blog), 7 July 2020.
what_it_supplies: the front's composition: the swell bay at the north end, the forward wing at the south end, the entrance between them
the storey lines: a raised basement, a principal floor about 2.3 m over grade, a second floor about 6.6 m, the cornice about 11.5 m
the roof: steep and slated, two gabled dormers on the street face and one on the north face, two tall stacks on the north wall and one on the wing
the openings: three windows a storey in the bay, one a storey in the wing, one over the door
what_it_does_not_supply: colour: the print is monochrome, so the brick's and the trim's colours stay reconstructed
the south wall, the rear and the roof behind the street face
a date: undated, and its 1904 reading rests on Spalding's long ownership and nothing recorded as changing the front before the 1911 sheet

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 20.
what_it_supplies: The Illinois Central / Michigan Central right-of-way and, from the 16th Street row south about 60 m, the water's edge beside it, as of 1911
Footprints, lot lines, street widths (66 ft; 16th Street 50 ft), addresses, material by colour and story counts for Indiana Av. to the tracks, 16th to 18th Street, as of 1911
Its own printed Scale of Feet, which the georeference uses as its scale
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: T-2441 (piece 1 of T-1870) refines the district draft (T-2335) in place under the same id from the house's one picture of its remodelled front, a line engraving of the Grosvenor house as Jesse Spalding remodelled it (glessner_blog_1637_spalding_remodel_engraving), read against the 1911 Sanborn sheet 20, which controls the plan. The main body is rebuilt on the K01 frontage assembly at the sheet's own width (13.1 m, where the draft's fit had stopped at 11.5 m) and depth: a K03 brick block of a raised basement and two tall storeys under a bracketed cornice; at the north end of the front a K08 swell bay of three windows a storey rising nearly to the cornice, at the south end the wing the engraving draws forward of the front as a K08 full-height projection on the sheet's 4.8 m by 1.0 m step, the entrance up its stoop between them under one window; a slated mansard whose steep lower faces carry two dormers on the street face and one on the north face, and the three stacks the engraving draws. The sheet's two-storey rear range behind the south part stands on K01's rear wings. What the engraving shows and K01 cannot yet build, or this piece has not yet built, is listed open in its match record (data/reference_views/spalding_house_1637_prairie/spalding_remodel_engraving.match.json) for T-2442. T-2465 carries the wing up to the cornice under its own steep hip, its ridge running back into the main roof and its stack beside the ridge (K01's mansard crown built as a hip). T-2471 dresses the three stacks with the K15 kit's head (corbelled courses, a stone cap and, on the two tall ones, a sunk panel). Everything not read is reconstructed and recorded as L-k01-1637-spalding-remodel-2441. T-2467 carries K10's bracketed cornice round the wing under its crown and stands the engraving's block in it over the window.
